findings.claim: The collision was 15 divergent names, not one. Beyond SIGNAL/SIGNAL_HOVER/SIGNAL_PRESS it covered six neutrals (VOID, NEAR_BLACK, CARBON, GRAPHITE, SLATE, SILVER), BOTH type families (JetBrains Mono vs Space Mono, DM Sans vs Space Grotesk, plus their two CSS forms) and two panel dimensions (PANEL_MIN_HEIGHT 400 vs the ratified 420, PANEL_PREF_WIDTH 320 vs 340). The bridge silently reverted the Mile-1b height ruling.
findings.anchor: python/synapse/panel/tokens.py vs python/synapse/panel/designsystem/tokens.py, diffed by import under hython3.13

findings.claim: There were NINE colour-declaring sites, not two. The bridge, the design system, the off-repo ~/.synapse/design file, and six call-site `except ImportError` arms each holding a private palette. context_bar.py's was a Material-ish set (FIRE #e8833a, GROW #4caf50, WARN #ff9800, ERROR #f44336) matching NEITHER other authority — a context bar rendered under it showed a status grammar that exists nowhere else in the product.
findings.anchor: python/synapse/panel/context_bar.py (pre-change fallback arm); same shape in apex_recipes, recipe_book, error_translator, command_palette, message_formatter

findings.claim: Those fallback arms were REACHABLE, so they were live third states rather than dead code. Loading panel/apex_recipes.py by path with synapse off sys.path executes the arm and yields _SIGNAL = #00D4FF. Classified before removal (Law 4): no caller in python/ or tests/ loads a panel module by path, so the arms had no user and their only observable effect was painting a different design system.
findings.anchor: probe: hython3.13 spec_from_file_location('ar','python/synapse/panel/apex_recipes.py') with SYNAPSE paths stripped -> 'STANDALONE LOAD OK; _SIGNAL= #00D4FF'
findings.disposition: removed rather than corrected — a standalone load now fails loudly instead of silently rendering the wrong accent (Law 3). Escalated as H4.R2 because deleting a degradation path is a judgement call.

findings.claim: The bridge's fallback literals were not a faithful copy of the source they stood in for: NEAR_BLACK was #3A3A3A in the fallback and #3C3C3C in the live off-repo file. Reading the except-arm was never reading the panel, which is why a source-only census of this defect is untrustworthy and the runtime diff was necessary.

SIZE_HERO's live value is 19, in every import path. The 44 at tokens.py:59 sat in the off-repo fallback block and was overwritten unconditionally by the designsystem import a few lines later, so it could not survive to be read even when the fallback ran. The same held for all six SIZE_* fallback assignments.
findings.disposition: fixed — the whole ambiguity is gone; the scale has one source and cannot be double-assigned

findings.claim: THE METHOD FINDING, and it hit three readers including two I wrote. (a) L4's own token oracle assert_panel_tokens.py matched ALIAS-QUALIFIED strings ('t.VOID'), so an alias repoint read as a dropped token — and it would equally have PASSED a swap of one token for another behind the same alias. (b) My reader resolved relative imports globally: `from . import tokens` is the bridge in panel/ and the design system in panel/designsystem/, and the global rule reported all 21 of designsystem/qss.py's correct references as offenders — a repair driven by it would have edited a file that was never broken. (c) My reader walked only ast.Attribute, so context_bar's three getattr(_t, 'TEXT', default) reads were invisible.
findings.disposition: all three fixed, each with a named control: test_reader_resolves_a_relative_import_by_the_files_own_package, test_reader_sees_a_getattr_token_read, and assert_panel_tokens._selftest. Every one was found by pointing the reader at the tree and READING the output instead of believing it.

findings.claim: Three consent-honesty checks could not run at all on the shipping interpreter. tests/panel/test_gate_consent_honesty.py used object.__new__(GateWidget); a Shiboken type refuses it. Under stock python the file never ran (no PySide6) so the defect was invisible; under hython3.13 all three errored before reaching a single assertion. A safety check that cannot execute is Law 1 wearing a green coat.
findings.disposition: fixed (GateWidget.__new__). Three consent checks now actually run and pass.

findings.claim: synapse_panel.py had no module logger, so _wire_gate's `except Exception: pass` swallowed a consent-relay wiring failure in silence — if that relay fails, a raised gate stops bringing the Review face forward and the artist is asked to approve something they are not shown. My first fix used logger.debug and was itself a decoration: the panel's own bootstrap calls ensure_file_logging(), which sets the `synapse` logger to INFO, so a debug record on that path is discarded in EVERY live session. The test that demanded the trail was also order-dependent — it passed alone and failed after any test that builds a panel, for exactly this reason.
findings.disposition: fixed at WARNING, and the test now pins the `synapse` logger to its PRODUCTION level for the duration — which makes it stricter and order-independent, not looser.

findings.claim: TWO OF MY OWN INSTRUMENTS WERE DEFECTIVE and a hostile review caught both. (a) panel_shot.py applied no stylesheet, so six of sixteen standalone views rendered on Qt's DEFAULT LIGHT chrome (#EFEFEF backgrounds) — a shot set that looked like evidence and showed a panel no artist has seen. (b) panel_accent_census.py gated on exact matches at +-8 while its docstring claimed 'point any panel view at #00D4FF and the CYAN row goes non-zero'. False: context_bar and hda_describe were both bound to the cyan in source and both scored ZERO, because small antialiased glyph strokes never reach the pure colour (context_bar: 0 within +-8, 2 within +-24, 31 within +-48). A leg could have claimed a clean sweep with cyan text still on screen.
findings.disposition: both fixed. The shot harness now applies qss.stylesheet() to every view; the census reports a tolerance ladder (8/24/48), gates on the widest band, refuses to report if its own control fails, and documents what the wide band cannot discriminate. BOTH screenshot sets were then re-shot with the corrected instrument.

for_ruling.question: The oracle clause `grep -c 't\.SIGNAL' python/synapse/panel/*.py -> 0` is not met (returns 12), and I believe the clause is measuring the wrong thing rather than the code being wrong. All 12 bind the alias to the design system. Accept the semantic pin in its place, or require the textual rename?
options: Accept the semantic pin (test_no_panel_module_binds_the_bridge_for_a_shared_colour) as the governing form and retire the grep clause
Require the textual rename: `t` -> `_ds` across six files so the grep returns 0
Keep both: rename, AND keep the semantic pin
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1. The grep cannot distinguish `t`=bridge from `t`=designsystem, which is precisely the uncalibrated-reader failure R60 rules on — applied here to the oracle itself. Renaming six already-correct files would give one module two alias names, the exact shadow this leg removed from styles.py, for zero semantic gain. But this is your call, not mine: I did not rewrite the oracle to suit the work, which is why the leg is amber.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: None functional. The collision is closed and pinned either way; this decides how the clause is written in future briefs.

for_ruling.question: Six call-site `except ImportError` arms held private palettes. They were reachable (a by-path load runs them) but unused (no caller in the tree loads a panel module by path). I DELETED them, so a standalone by-path load now raises instead of rendering a different design system. Correct trade?
options: Confirm deletion — fail loudly beats rendering the wrong accent silently
Restore the arms but source them from the design system by path
Restore them as-is and accept the extra palettes
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1, which is what shipped. Law 3 says a path that cannot do the thing should raise, not succeed wrongly, and a palette that silently disagrees with the product is the same class of defect as a consent gate that does not gate (R18). Option 2 was attempted and abandoned: designsystem/tokens.py uses a relative import for its theme seam, so it cannot be loaded by path without package context, and the retry dance was more machinery than the degradation path was worth.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Low. Reversible in one commit if a real by-path consumer surfaces.

for_ruling.question: CONIFEROUS #6E8F72 landed as specified and is a measured contrast reduction (3.988 vs 6.506 against PANEL). It is fine for the status dots it mostly colours (WCAG 3:1 non-text) but sits below the 4.5 AA text floor at designsystem/qss.py:121, where it colours a DsVerb button LABEL. Keep, lighten, or restrict?
options: Keep the spec value everywhere — the muted family already lives in this band (NO_SOFT 4.257)
Keep CONIFEROUS for dots, use a lighter variant for the DsVerb text usage
Lighten CONIFEROUS itself until it clears 4.5 against PANEL
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 2 if you want the numbers clean, Option 1 if the verb tone is meant to read as quiet. I have deliberately not chosen: the value is a design decision and Article I keeps an agent out of 'what a number should be'. What I can tell you is the measurement, which nobody had.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Low, and bounded — it affects one button tone.

for_ruling.question: The seeded-contrast sweep still covers only the body and secondary roles. MUSHROOM (L4.R4) and now CONIFEROUS are both outside it. Extend the sweep to every text-carrying colour token?
options: Extend the sweep to all text-carrying tokens
Leave it — the two new tokens were hand-measured
Extend, and add a rule that a new text token cannot land without sweep coverage
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 3. L4 recommended Option 1 three days ago and the gap grew by one token in the meantime, which is the argument for making the coverage requirement structural rather than remembered. This is the second leg to hand-measure a token because the gate could not.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Grows by one blind spot per new text token.

for_ruling.question: The off-repo ~/.synapse/design side channel is no longer read by product code — the reproducibility defect R21 deposited is closed for the panel. But tests/test_design_system.py still loads that directory directly (with a staleness guard), and design/tokens.py + design/synapse_styles.py in-repo still mirror the old palette. Retire the parallel design tree, or keep it as a design-authoring surface?
options: Retire the parallel tree; the vendored design system is the product's only design source
Keep it as an authoring/export surface and add a conformance test against the vendored tokens
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 2. The tree is not harmful now that no product code reads it, but two files claiming to be the design system with different values is how this defect started, and a conformance test is the cheap version of the fix. Out of scope for H4 — flagged, not touched.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Low now that the product no longer reads it.
